title: Driver Dispatch & Proof of Delivery
notes:
Discovery call — Driver dispatch & proof-of-delivery platform — 10 Feb 2026

Karan Malhotra (Head of Operations): We run about 3,500 deliveries a day across Bangalore and Hyderabad with roughly 220 riders. Right now dispatch is done manually by hub coordinators looking at a spreadsheet — we need the system to auto-assign the nearest available rider to each order.

Neha Iyer (Product Owner): The auto-assignment needs to consider both distance and current rider load — someone with three pending drops shouldn't get a fourth if there's a free rider two streets away.

Ravi Kumar (Fleet Manager): Riders need a mobile app that shows their route for the day, and it must work with patchy network — a lot of our delivery zones have poor connectivity. The app should queue updates offline and sync when signal comes back.

Karan Malhotra (Head of Operations): Proof of delivery is critical — every delivery needs a photo and either a signature or an OTP entered by the customer before it's marked complete. We had a spike in "item not received" disputes last quarter and it cost us badly on chargebacks.

Neha Iyer (Product Owner): Ideally the OTP should be sent to the customer automatically via SMS when the rider is within, say, 500 meters of the drop location.

Sameer Qureshi (Engineering Lead): For live tracking, the customer-facing tracking link needs to update the rider's location at least every 30 seconds. Our maps and routing run on the Google Maps Platform, that's already contracted.

Ravi Kumar (Fleet Manager): Failed deliveries need a reason code — customer not available, wrong address, refused — and those should automatically trigger a reattempt the next day, up to two attempts before we return it to the hub.

Karan Malhotra (Head of Operations): We also need this to integrate with our existing order management system, Unicommerce, so that order status updates flow back there in real time. We're not replacing Unicommerce.

Sameer Qureshi (Engineering Lead): On scale, during the festive peak we hit 9,000 deliveries in a single day. The dispatch engine has to assign a rider within 10 seconds of an order coming in, even at that peak.

Neha Iyer (Product Owner): Route optimization across an entire hub's deliveries — like solving the best order to visit 40 stops — is out of scope for this phase. We're doing single-order assignment only for now, batch routing is a phase two thing.

Ravi Kumar (Fleet Manager): One more constraint — riders are contract workers with their own phones, mostly older Android devices, so the app has to run acceptably on low-end Android, we can't assume everyone has a flagship phone.

Karan Malhotra (Head of Operations): Last month we had a rider go completely off-route for two hours and nobody noticed until the customer called to complain, that shouldn't be able to happen again.

Karan Malhotra (Head of Operations): We need this live before the next big sale event, which is roughly ten weeks out, and the finance team has capped spend at 35 lakh for build plus first year of maps API costs.
